questions.stem: On a sample assessment, 594 - How many positive divisors does 594 have?

options.misconception: it adds a phantom divisor
it counts only divisors up to the square root
it assumes every smaller number divides n

questions.explanation: Factor 594 and apply the divisor-counting rule: the number of positive divisors is the product of one more than each prime exponent, which gives 16. Choice B is a distractor: it adds a phantom divisor. Choice C is a distractor: it counts only divisors up to the square root. Choice D is a distractor: it assumes every smaller number divides n.
questions.hint: Use the prime factorization to count divisors.

questions.stem: For a group activity, 415 - How many positive divisors does 415 have?

options.misconception: it adds a phantom divisor
it counts only divisors up to the square root
it assumes every smaller number divides n

questions.explanation: Factor 415 and apply the divisor-counting rule: the number of positive divisors is the product of one more than each prime exponent, which gives 4. questions.hint: Use the prime factorization to count divisors.
